caption:
Best designer bags under $2500 ⬇️

These are the bags I would recommend & why!

- Saint Laurent Kate Bag: This is a great little bag that works for both day and night. Wear it as a crossbody bag or on the shoulder. Both the medium & small sizes are under $2500. The WOC is also a great option!

- Gucci GG Marmont Shoulder Bag: A practical everyday crossbody bag that’s quiet roomy for a small bag - definitely fits all the essentials.

- Louis Vuitton Neverfull MM: You can’t go wrong with a good tote! This is a great designer bag for work & both the canvas & leather versions come in at under $2500.

- Celine Nano Belt Bag: This is one of my long-time favourite Celine bags! It’s compact but fits a decent amount and I love that it also has a top handle.

- Fendi Baguette Mini: This is a great entry piece if you love mini bags & you’re looking for your first Fendi bag. 

- Celine Nano Luggage bag: I had to put this one on the list - it’s one of my old favourites that I still love & use to this day! I love a crossbody bag that also has a top handle - they are just so practical! This one fits SO much for a small bag.

Let me know your picks in the comments!

#baglover #bagcollection #luxurybags #designerbags #wardrobegoals #closetgoals #closetorganization

When people imagine packing for ten days in Europe, they often picture ten outfits.

In reality, the goal is much simpler: build a small wardrobe where everything works together.

Instead of thinking in outfits, I plan in layers and combinations. A few well-chosen pieces can create far more than ten looks once you start mixing them thoughtfully.

When I’m packing for a trip like this, I walk through a simple framework:
• Start with a base palette. Choose two or three core colors so everything mixes easily.�• Add layers that cooperate. A knit, a blazer, and a coat should all work together comfortably.�• Choose bottoms that repeat well. Trousers, denim, or a skirt that can anchor multiple outfits.�• Pack shoes that support the itinerary. One true walking shoe, one polished option, and one that slightly elevates the wardrobe.�• Make sure every piece works at least three ways.

Once those pieces are in place, the combinations come naturally. Getting dressed becomes easy because everything already belongs together.

This is exactly the approach I used to create my Spring in Europe: The Style + Packing Guide.

Inside the 47-page guide, I’ve taken the guesswork out of it. Along with curated packing picks across categories like sweaters, tops, and shoes, I’ve styled seven complete suitcases so you can see exactly how everything works together before you even zip your bag.

caption:
Packing properly is a sport. 

Over a long time, I’ve refined my packing process into a few simple rules that make getting dressed abroad so much easier:

▪️The 3-Color Rule: Stick to a palette of three colors that play well together.

▪️The 1:3 Ratio: Every hero piece—like a blazer or a pair of boots—must work with three different outfits.

▪️Smart Accessories: Lean on “repeatable” items like a classic neutral belt or a versatile scarf for a pop of color that works with your color palette. 

▪️Play Dress Up: Try on your options while you pack. It’s the only way to really lock in your styling strategy. (Serious packing guru, @heleneisfor, even goes so far to take selfies of each look.)

▪️Great jeans: enough said.
